svg.title: How this plugin fits into DSH and Perplexity
svg.desc: Three horizontal layers — the DSH host, this plugin, and the Perplexity API — crossed by two capability lanes. The web search lane backs the host's own web_search tool: the plugin registers a provider into the ctx.web seam, which calls Perplexity's Agent API by default or its Search API when selected. The research lane adds a tool this plugin owns, with its own 30-minute budget, plus a skill that is guidance for the model rather than a call, and always reaches Perplexity through the Agent API. Of Perplexity's four published APIs (Router, Agent, Search, Embeddings) only two are in scope.
svg.text: How this plugin fits into DSH and Perplexity
One plugin, two distinct capabilities: a web-search backend the host's own tool uses, and research the plugin owns.
Web search lane
Research lane

DSH host
the host owns the model-facing tools; this plugin supplies one backend and one extra tool
Web search — the host's tool, backed by this plugin
web_search — the model-facing tool. Owned by dsh-tool-web, not by this plugin.
budget: the session's tool-web.searchTimeoutMs (60 s shipped) — the host enforces it
this plugin supplies the provider behind it, registered into ctx.web
so the tool the model already knows keeps working unchanged
Research — a tool and a skill this plugin adds
perplexity_research — a tool we contribute; it declares its own timeoutMs
budget: researchTimeoutMs, 30 minutes by default — ours, not the host's
skill perplexity-research — markdown loaded into the model's context:
when to search vs research, how to read a degraded result, how to cite

{ content, sources[], truncated }
+ degradation · images on the seam object

no request of its own, no budget of its own, no vendor dependency
the research tool is what actually calls the API, one layer below
This plugin — @shjwudp/dsh-web-search-perplexity
① Provider adapter — the web-search backend
perplexity→ Agent API (default)
perplexity-search→ Search API (opt-in)
selected by searchProvider; only the selected one reports available()
it adds no second search tool — it backs the one the host already has
so switching backends never changes the agent's tool list
② Research orchestrator · ③ the skill
toolperplexity_research — submits, polls, cancels
skillperplexity-research — guidance for the model
config: researchDepth (low · medium · high · wide) · researchTimeoutMs
the tool always runs through the Agent API, whatever searchProvider selects
its budget, its depth ladder, and its own failure class
Shared — transport and configuration (src/shared.js · src/agent-run.js · src/client.js)
background submit + poll; cancel the run when a deadline expires; 429 → capped backoff with a full diagnostic
connection failure → cause chain, HTTP method, pid and uptime; degraded retry, marked machine-readably; image guards
web search → Agent API (default), or Search API (opt-in)
POST /v1/agent { input, tools, preset, background: true }
POST /search { query, max_results, filters }
one of the two per call — never both
research → Agent API only
POST /v1/agent { input, tools, preset, background: true }
then GET /v1/agent/{id} until the status is terminal
no Search API path: it returns results, not an answer
Perplexity API
four published surfaces — two of them are in scope here
Router
outside scope
Agent API
in scope · default
Search API
in scope · opt-in
Embeddings
outside scope
Agent API
POST /v1/agentsubmit with background: true
GET /v1/agent/{id}poll until the status is terminal
POST /v1/agent/{id}/cancelwhen a deadline expires
presets: fast · low · medium · high · xhigh · wide-research
returns output[]: the answer message + search_results[]; takes input_image
Search API
POST /search
returns results[] only — no generated answer
max_results · domains · languages · country
publication dates · recency · search_type: people
selected with searchProvider: perplexity-search

Out of scope here: Router serves open-weight models through OpenAI- and Anthropic-compatible endpoints, and Embeddings produces vectors. Neither answers a question; Sonar, the Agent API's predecessor, is supported until 2026-09-27.
Scope of this diagram: the host → plugin → vendor paths for web search and long-running research. Internal implementation, the complete configuration reference, and unused APIs are omitted.
